args.title: aca-redline.docx
args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — COUNTERPARTY DRAFT
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE

Prepared by: Contracts Review Team
Matter: Deal materials — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
Date: [Current Date]

_____________________________________________________________________________

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This redline addresses the counterparty's markup against the firm's standard Account Control Agreement (ACA) form and applicable market precedent. Three material deviations have been identified and are marked for revision below:

1. Indemnification Cap Reduction (Section 6.2)
2. Material Adverse Effect Definition Carve-outs (Section 1.1)
3. Representation Survival Shortening (Section 8.3)

All revisions are shown in tracked-changes format with rationale notes. Accepted provisions are unmarked.

_____________________________________________________________________________

II. INDEMNIFICATION CAP AND BASKET — SECTION 6.2

[COUNTERPARTY DRAFT - MARKED FOR REVISION]

CURRENT (Counterparty) Language:
"Indemnification Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the total aggregate liability of [Counterparty] under all indemnification obligations shall not exceed the lesser of (a) the then-current balance of the Controlled Account, or (b) $[X] million ¶ Basket. Losses shall be subject to a tipping basket of $[Y] (the 'Basket'), whereby indemnification obligations shall not apply until aggregate Losses exceed the Basket amount, at which time [Counterparty] shall be liable for all Losses in excess of the Basket."

FIRM POSITION - REQUIRED REVISION:
"Indemnification Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the total aggregate liability of [Counterparty] under all indemnification obligations shall not exceed the lesser of (a) the then-current balance of the Controlled Account, or (b) $[X] million ¶ Basket. Losses shall be subject to a deductible basket of $[Y] (the 'Basket'), whereby indemnification obligations shall not apply unless and until aggregate Losses exceed the Basket amount; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, that once the Basket is exceeded, [Counterparty] shall be liable for Losses in excess of the Basket amount. [¶ COMMENT: Deductible (dollar-one) recovery structure is firm standard; tipping basket creates exposure by shifting first-dollar recovery of all losses above basket to [Counterparty] once threshold is breached. Tipping baskets are off-market in the banking context and expose our client to recovery uncertainty. This revision restores deductible treatment.]"

_____________________________________________________________________________

III. MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT DEFINITION — SECTION 1.1

[COUNTERPARTY DRAFT - MARKED FOR REVISION]

CURRENT (Counterparty) Language:
"Material Adverse Effect" shall mean any event, change, or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, assets, liabilities, or financial condition of [Counterparty]; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, that a Material Adverse Effect shall not include any adverse effect resulting from: (a) general economic or capital market conditions; (b) changes in law of general applicability; (c) regulatory actions or enforcement proceedings conducted by any bank regulator; or (d) any event or circumstance disclosed in the disclosure schedules."

FIRM POSITION - REQUIRED REVISION:
"Material Adverse Effect" shall mean any event, change, or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, assets, liabilities, or financial condition of [Counterparty]; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, that a Material Adverse Effect shall not include any adverse effect resulting from: (a) general economic or capital market conditions; (b) changes in law of general applicability; or (c) ¶ any event or circumstance disclosed in the disclosure schedules. [¶ COMMENT: Counterparty's carve-out for 'regulatory actions or enforcement proceedings conducted by any bank regulator' is unacceptable. This language eliminates MAE protection precisely where [Counterparty]'s regulatory status is most at risk. This carve-out is directly contrary to the engagement facts (regulatory issue at the core of this matter) and removes a key covenant protection. Delete subsection (c) in its entirety. The MAE definition must preserve our client's ability to rely on regulatory stability of the counterparty as a material condition.]"

_____________________________________________________________________________

IV. REPRESENTATION SURVIVAL PERIOD — SECTION 8.3

[COUNTERPARTY DRAFT - MARKED FOR REVISION]

CURRENT (Counterparty) Language:
"Survival of Representations. The representations and warranties of [Counterparty] contained in this Agreement or in any certificate delivered pursuant hereto shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until 5:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, at which time such representations and warranties shall expire and be of no further force or effect; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, that the representations and warranties in Sections [5.1, 5.2, 5.3] (fundamental representations regarding authority, organization, and capitalization) shall survive until sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations."

FIRM POSITION - REQUIRED REVISION:
"Survival of Representations. The representations and warranties of [Counterparty] contained in this Agreement or in any certificate delivered pursuant hereto shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until 5:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on the date that is three (3) years ¶ [strike: eighteen (18) months] after the Closing Date, at which time such representations and warranties shall expire and be of no further force or effect; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, that the representations and warranties in Sections [5.1, 5.2, 5.3] (fundamental representations regarding authority, organization, and capitalization) shall survive until sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. [¶ COMMENT: Eighteen-month survival for standard representations is materially below market in account control agreements and depository arrangements. Three-year survival is firm standard and aligns with regulatory expectations for account control documentation. The extended survival for fundamental representations is acceptable. This revision is essential to ensure adequate time for discovery of potential breaches in a depository context where timing of detection may be delayed.]"

_____________________________________________________________________________

V. SECTION-BY-SECTION CLEAN-UP

All other sections of the counterparty's draft are acceptable and require no revision, subject to the following technical conforming corrections:

[Section references and minor conforming edits to cross-references as revised above]

_____________________________________________________________________________

VI. DELIVERABLE SIGN-OFF

This redline incorporates all firm-standard protections and market-baseline requirements for Account Control Agreements in the banking/depository context. The three marked revisions address material deviations from:

1. Firm Standard ACA Playbook (Indemnification/Basket structure)
2. Regulatory Expectations (MAE carve-outs)
3. Market Precedent (Representation Survival periods)

All marked revisions should be presented to counterparty as negotiating positions with supporting market precedent. Accept no further modifications to the three flagged sections without senior partner review.

_____________________________________________________________________________
END OF REDLINE
